instruction: coordinator, 2026-09-26, relaying Paul (owner) verbatim: "we are USING THE 538 DATA IN THE Markdown" and "authorize everything"; downloads from official 538 sources authorized. Task: fetch the official 538 generic-ballot data (GitHub congress-generic-ballot folder; projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/data/generic_ballot_averages.csv, Wayback of the same URL if dead), compute the within-year annual mean of the D-R margin 2008-2026, write sheet expected_control_538 (House vote-intention margin, robustness only); optional 2018-2024 forecast P(Dem control) Lite/Classic/Deluxe. Existing sheets and cells bit-exact; append without re-serialising existing parts.

method.generic_ballot:
Parsing and annual aggregation of the two official 538 generic-ballot files (shared by compute and build).

Daily margin = Democratic estimate - Republican estimate (points), one value per date.
  - generic_topline_historical.csv (GitHub, fivethirtyeight/data/congress-generic-ballot): columns subgroup,
    modeldate (M/D/YYYY), dem_estimate, rep_estimate, ...; subgroup is "All polls" on every row; one row per date.
  - generic_ballot_averages.csv (projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/data, archived): columns candidate
    (Democrats/Republicans), pct_estimate, lo, hi, date (YYYY-MM-DD), election, cycle; one Democrats and one
    Republicans row per date.
Annual value = statistics.mean (exact) of the daily margins dated inside the calendar year; no interpolation, no
carry-forward, no weighting; n_days = dates used; first/last date = first and last of them.
method.control: P(Dem control): 2018 win_probability of party D; 2020/2022 chamber_Dparty; one run per date x model; within-year unweighted mean over the forecast dates (all are in the election year, on or before election day)

edit_method: zip-level append: one new worksheet part; workbook.xml, workbook.xml.rels, [Content_Types].xml and the notes/dictionary/sources/coverage sheet parts changed only by insertion (each proven equal to the original after removing the insertion); all other parts byte-identical; every pre-existing cell compared by type and repr (openpyxl read-only) against the backup
